ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, and point $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$. If $AC=6$, what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Since $AB=AC$ and $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, \\
it follows that $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$, \\
Since $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$, \\
it follows that $DE$ is the median of the triangle, \\
Given $AC=6$, \\
it follows that $DE=\boxed{3}$.

method.method_draft: Use the midpoint-segment theorem. First read the diagram as triangle ABC with A at the top, B and C on the base, D lying on segment BC, E lying on segment AB, and segment DE drawn. From the text, AB=AC and AD bisects angle BAC, so in the isosceles triangle the angle bisector from A to the base also makes D the midpoint of BC. The text also states E is the midpoint of AB. Therefore DE connects the midpoints of two sides of triangle ABC, so by the midsegment theorem DE is parallel to AC and has length half of AC. Since AC=6, DE=3.
